safi-cedvel:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of the oath; (الكتاب) genitive by the wāw, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم"; (في ليلة) attached to (أنزلناه) ...
The clause «(أقسم) بالكتاب ...» has no grammatical position: inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّا أنزلناه ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the oath.
The clause «أنزلناه ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «كنّا منذرين ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the (second) إنّ.
4- 5- (فيها) attached to the passive (يفرق); (أمرا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with it in meaning, i.e. a distinguishing [Note: Or in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of أنزلناه, or of its object, or of the fāʿil of يفرق.. or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) governed by أنزلنا or منذرين or يفرق.]; (من عندنا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (أمرا).
The clause «يفرق كلّ أمر ...» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of ليلة.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(رحمة) an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi [Note: Or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of مرسلين, or a badal (substitute) of (أمرا).]; (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt of (رحمة); (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is السميع, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.].
The clause «إنّه ... السميع ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
(ربّ) a badal of ربّك, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات; (بينهما) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (كنتم) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «كنتم موقنين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or parenthetical.] ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: then be certain of the message of Muhammad, upon him be peace.
8- (ربّكم) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "(الله)", in the position of nominative.. or a second khabar of the particle resembling the verb, إنّ.].
The clause «يحيى ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or it is a khabar after a khabar, and likewise the clause (هو) ربّكم.].
The clause «يميت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحيى.
The clause «(هو) ربّكم ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); (في شكّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
The clause «هم في شكّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يلعبون ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Benefits:
- بل ...
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ. (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); the meaning of iḍrāb is that you negate the judgement of what precedes it and affirm it for what follows it, as in: جاء زيد بل عمرو. We shall clarify some matters related to it:
1- It is a particle of digression. If a clause follows it, the sense of the digression is either cancellation (ibṭāl), as in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ وَلَداً سُبْحانَهُ، بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ, i.e. rather they are servants; (بل) has cancelled the judgement that the All-Merciful has taken a son. And as in the words of Allah the Exalted: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ؟ بَلْ جاءَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ.
Or it conveys transition from one purpose to another, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى. وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى. بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا, and ولَدَيْنا كِتابٌ يَنْطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ. In all of this it is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), not a conjunction, according to the correct view.
2- If a single word follows it, it is a conjunction. Then, if a command or an affirmation precedes it — (اضرب زيدا بل عمرا) and (قام زيد بل عمرو) — nothing is judged about what precedes it, and the judgement is affirmed for what follows it.
3- If a negation or prohibition precedes it, it serves to confirm what precedes it as it is and to assign its opposite to what follows it, as in «ما قام زيد بل عمرو» and «لا يقم زيد بل عمرو».
4- «لا» is added before it to reinforce the digression after an affirmation, as in the saying of the poet:
وجهك البدر لا بل الشمس لو لم ... يقض للشمس كسفة أو أفول
(Your face is the full moon — no, rather the sun, had eclipse or setting not been decreed for the sun.)
When it occurs after a negation, it reinforces the confirmation of what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive, for linking; (يوم) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بدخان) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأتي), and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya).
The clause «ارتقب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a resumption caused by what preceded, i.e.: take heed, and watch.
The clause «تأتي السماء ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يغشي ...» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of دخان.
The clause «هذا عذاب ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb, i.e.: they said: this is a punishment.
The clause «ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «اكشف عنّا ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّا مؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Benefits:
- Some of the signs of the Resurrection.
It is narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ saw the disbelievers of Mecca turning away, he said:
O Allah, [send] seven [years] like the seven of Yūsuf. Then a year [of drought] seized them which destroyed everything, until they ate hides and carrion from hunger, and one of them would look at the sky and see something like smoke. Then Abū Sufyān came to him and said: You have come commanding obedience to Allah and the maintaining of kinship ties, and your people have perished, so pray to Allah for them.
So he prayed, and Allah removed the punishment from them; then they reverted, so He took vengeance on them on the day of Badr, as shown by the words of Allah the Exalted: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرى إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ.
It is also said that it is a smoke that will come before the Hour is established and has not yet come. It will enter the ears of the disbelievers and the hypocrites until a man's head becomes like a roasted (ḥanīdh, grilled) head, while the believer will be afflicted by something like a cold, and the whole earth will be like a house in which a fire has been kindled. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: so in the source; probably "Ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḥasan"]. It is supported by what al-Baghawī narrated with the chain of al-Thaʿlabī from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The first of the signs (i.e. the signs of the Hour) are the descent of ʿĪsā son of Maryam, and a fire that will come out of the depths of ʿAdan driving people to the place of gathering, taking its midday rest (sleeping) with them when they take their midday rest. Ḥudhayfa said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is the smoke?
So he recited this verse يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّماءُ بِدُخانٍ مُبِينٍ: it will fill what is between the east and the west and remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, something like a cold will afflict him from it; and as for the disbeliever, he will be like one drunk; it will come out of his nostrils, his ears and his backside.
And Allah knows best. The meaning of حصّت is: destroyed.

safi-cedvel:13-16.t:
* I'rab:
(أنّى) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: Or it is an adverb governed by the sense of "being established" (al-istiqrār), and the khabar is (لهم).]; (لهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الذكرى; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
The clause «أنّى لهم الذكرى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاءهم رسول ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the pronoun in (لهم).
14- (تولّوا) indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; (عنه) attached to (تولّوا); (معلّم) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو"; (مجنون) a nominative second khabar.
The clause «تولّوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause جاءهم رسول.
The clause «قالوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause جاءهم رسول [Note: Or it is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of تولّوا, with قد implied.].
The clause «(هو) معلّم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
15- (قليلا) an accusative noun standing in for an implied adverb (ẓarf), i.e. a little time [Translator's note: the source has طرف, evidently a misprint for ظرف.] [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. a little removal.] ...
The clause «إنّا كاشفوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), an answer to their supplication ...
The clause «إنّكم عائدون ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding resumption.
16- (يوم) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (عائدون) [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر".]; (البطشة) an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.
The clause «نبطش ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّا منتقمون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption — or causal —.

* Morphology:
(14) معلّم: passive participle of the four-letter علّم; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(15) عائدون: plural of عائد, active participle of the triliteral عاد; its pattern is فاعل. It contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the weak letter by hamza: its original form is عاود; the wāw came after the alif of فاعل and was changed to hamza, as is regular in the active participle of hollow verbs.
(16) البطشة: a maṣdar of a single occurrence (al-marra) of the triliteral verb بطش; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:17-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (قبلهم) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فتنا); the wāw is a conjunction — or circumstantial —.
The clause «قد فتنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
The clause «جاءهم رسول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the oath [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد implied.].
18- (أن) explicative (tafsīriyya), because something carrying the sense of speech precedes it [Note: It may be maṣdar-forming, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive by an omitted bāʾ, i.e. بأن أدّوا, the preposition being attached to (جاءهم).. It may also be lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause أدّوا the khabar of أنّ.]; (إليّ) attached to (أدّوا); (عباد) an accusative vocative (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and the object of (أدّوا) is omitted; (لكم) attached to a ḥāl of رسول.
The clause «أدّوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «the vocative and its implied answer» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّي لكم رسول ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding command — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
19- (الواو) conjunction; (أن) like the first, in all its possibilities; (لا) prohibitive; (على الله) attached to (تعلوا); (آتيكم) a nominative khabar (predicate) of إنّ, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ [Note: It is an active participle — or it is a nominative imperfect verb, (كم) being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the clause the khabar of إنّ.]; (بسلطان) attached to (آتيكم) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in آتيكم.].
The clause «لا تعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «إنّي آتيكم ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding prohibition — or an explanatory resumption.
20- (الواو) resumptive; (بربّي) attached to (عذت); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-making particle; the nūn in (ترجمون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted to suit the verse-ending (fāṣila).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ترجمون) is in the position of genitive [Translator's note: the source reads "in the position of a preposition", evidently a slip for "genitive".] by an omitted preposition, attached to (عذت), i.e. from your stoning me.
The clause «إنّي عذت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عذت ...» is the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ترجمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
21- (الواو) conjunction; (لم) for negation only; (تؤمنوا) a jussive imperfect verb, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (لي) attached to (تؤمنوا) by its being made to carry the meaning of تقرّوا "acknowledge" (taḍmīn); (الفاء) linking the apodosis; the (النون) in (اعتزلون) is for protection.
The clause «إن لم تؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّي عذت.
The clause «اعتزلون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with fāʾ.
22- (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «دعا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: they did not leave him alone, so he called upon his Lord.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ هؤلاء قوم..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (دعا), i.e.: he called upon his Lord with [the words] that these are a people.. and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya).

* Morphology:
(18) أدّوا: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, starting from the imperfect. Its imperfect assigned to the plural wāw is هم يؤدّون, originally يؤديون; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was moved to the dāl — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because, being vowelless, it met the plural wāw, so it became يؤدّون. When it passed to the imperative, the iʿlāl remained. The pattern of أدّوا is أفعوا.
(19) تعلوا: it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is تعلووا — with two wāws — and when two vowelless letters met, the wāw of the verb, the weak letter, was deleted and it became تعلوا; its pattern is تفعوا.
(آتيكم): active participle of the triliteral أتى, on the pattern فاعل. When the hamza of أتى met the alif of فاعل, they were merged and a madda was placed over them.. It contains iʿlāl by making vowelless, the original being آتيكم with ḍamma on the yāʾ..
The word may also be an imperfect of the triliteral أتى: when the hamza of the imperfect entered, the second hamza being vowelless, they were merged and the madda was placed over them; the original is أأتى with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بعبادي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسر); (ليلا) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (أسر); the adverb comes for emphasis.
The clause «أسر ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you want deliverance, then travel by night.. and the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb, i.e.: Allah the Exalted said to Mūsā ...
The clause «إنّكم متّبعون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
24- (الواو) conjunction; (رهوا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of البحر [Note: Or a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (اترك), if it is one of the verbs of transformation; al-ʿUkbarī said this.].
The clause «اترك ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أسر ...
The clause «إنّهم جند ...» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Morphology:
(رهوا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral رها يرهو, meaning "to be still" or "to part"; in the verse it is used in place of an adjective meaning "still" or "parted".

* Benefits:
- The hamza of the imperative.
The hamza of the imperative is a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) in the three-letter, five-letter and six-letter verbs. The three-letter, such as اكتب - انزل - اذهب.
The five-letter, such as: انتظم - ارتقب - احترس.
The six-letter, such as: استخدم - استغفر. It is to be noted that its vowel is kasra in the imperative, except for the three-letter verb with ḍamma on the ʿayn, where it comes with ḍamma, such as: اكتب - أرسم. Likewise it takes ḍamma in the imperfect of the five- and six-letter verbs in the passive [Translator's note: so in the source; the examples that follow are past passive forms.], such as: انتصر على العدو. استخدم الكتاب استخداما نافعا. As for the imperative of the four-letter verb beginning with a hamza, it is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), such as: أكرم - أحسن ... etc. It occurs in the verse under discussion: فأسر.

safi-cedvel:25-29.t:
* I'rab:
(كم) declarative (khabariyya), an allusive noun of number (kināya al-ʿadad), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من جنّات) tamyīz (specification); (فيها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فاكهين).
The clause «تركوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانوا فيها فاكهين» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of نعمة.
28- (كذلك) attached to the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus [Note: Or attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), governed by the verb تركوا or by an omitted verb, its implied form being "أهلكناهم" or "أخرجناهم".. In that case the clause أورثناها is conjoined to the implied clause.]; (الواو) conjunction; (قوما) an accusative second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «أورثناها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
29- (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (عليهم) attached to (بكت); (ما) "sufficing" (kāfiya) [Translator's note: so in the source; نافية "negative" is evidently meant.] in both places.
The clause «ما بكت عليهم السماء» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أورثناها.
The clause «ما كانوا منظرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to أورثناها.

* Morphology:
(29) بكت: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, the lām of the word and the tāʾ of the feminine.. its pattern is فعت.

* Rhetoric:
Imaginative representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ».
For the state of their death, because of its severity and magnitude, is likened to the state of one over whom the sky and the great celestial bodies weep. It is also said: it is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya), in that the sky and the earth are likened to a human being and weeping is attributed to them.
When an eminent man died, the Arabs would say, in magnifying his death: the sky and the earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the like. The poet said, lamenting the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
الشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة ... تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا
(The sun is risen, not eclipsed, weeping over you — [outshining] the stars of the night and the moon.)

* Benefits:
- In this verse occurs (كم) al-khabariyya (the declarative كم). We have spoken in detail about the interrogative كم and the declarative كم in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, verse (6), so refer back to it.

safi-cedvel:30-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) for realisation (taḥqīq); (من العذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نجّينا).
The clause «نجّينا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
31- (من فرعون) a badal (substitute) of العذاب with the preposition repeated; (من المسرفين) attached to a second khabar of (كان).
The clause «إنّه كان عاليا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
32- (ولقد) like the first, and the wāw is a conjunction; (على علم) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun; (على العالمين) attached to (اخترناهم) by its being made to carry the meaning of ميّزناهم "We distinguished them" (taḍmīn).
The clause «اخترناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.. the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first oath clause.
33- (الواو) conjunction; (من الآيات) attached to a ḥāl of (ما), which is the second object; (فيه) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of (بلاء).
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اخترناهم.
The clause «فيه بلاء ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Benefits:
- (ما) occurs in the noble verse in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَآتَيْناهُمْ مِنَ الْآياتِ ما فِيهِ بَلؤُا مُبِينٌ. (ما) here admits two readings: either it is a relative noun, or it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa) meaning "a thing". In both cases it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause after it is the ṣila in the first case and an adjective in the second. Ibn Hishām explained this aspect, saying: in our saying أعجبني ما صنعت, (ما) may mean الذي, or be an indefinite qualified noun — and on these two the resumptive pronoun is omitted, the implied form being أعجبني ما صنعته — or be maṣdar-forming, with no resumptive pronoun. Accordingly the implied sense is: "what you made pleased me", or "something you made", or "your making". These three readings occur in the words of Allah the Exalted: ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجاً مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ, i.e. of that which you decided, or of a thing you decided, or of your decision.
Ibn Hishām says: I do not know of them adding (ما) after the bāʾ except that its meaning is causal.
As in the words of Allah the Exalted: فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ and فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ.
As for (من), it sometimes admits being relative or qualified indefinite, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَما هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ; the implied sense is: among the people is he who says, or someone who says.

safi-cedvel:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative, governing like ليس; (منشرين) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ما ...
The clause «إنّ هؤلاء ليقولون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إن هي إلّا موتتنا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما نحن بمنشرين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause that is the object of speech.
36- (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بآبائنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ائتوا); (كنتم) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «ائتوا ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if you speak the truth, then bring ...
The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: explicative.. and the apodosis is implied, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(35) منشرين: plural of منشر, with ḍamma, then sukūn, then fatḥa; a passive participle of the four-letter أنشر; its pattern is مفعل.

safi-cedvel:37-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative, carrying the sense of rebuke; (أم) a conjunction; (قوم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the third-person pronoun هم; (الواو) resumptive — or conjunctive —; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It may be conjoined to (قوم) by the wāw, and the clause أهلكناهم is then a new sentence (mustaʾnafa).]; (من قبلهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause «هم خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أهلكناهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم كانوا مجرمين ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كانوا مجرمين ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
38- (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to السموات; (بينهما) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (لاعبين) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of خلقنا.
The clause «ما خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
39- (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of خلقناهما; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative.
The clause «ما خلقناهما ...» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of the clause ما خلقنا السموات.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما خلقناهما.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لكنّ.

* Morphology:
(تبّع): a proper name; he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, said to have been a prophet or a righteous man. Its pattern is فعّل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- Who is Tubbaʿ?
It is said: he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, one of the kings of Yemen, called Tubbaʿ because of the large number of his followers (atbāʿ). It is also said: it is a title of the kings of Yemen, just as [the ruler] is called caliph in Islam. Tubbaʿ used to worship fire; then he became Muslim and called his people Ḥimyar to Islam, but they denied him.
From Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Do not revile Tubbaʿ, for he had become Muslim. Narrated by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal.
From Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I do not know whether Tubbaʿ was a prophet or not a prophet.
From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: Do not revile Tubbaʿ, for he was a righteous man. Ibn Isḥāq and others mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās — they said: The last Tubbaʿ was Abū Karib Asʿad ibn Malīk. He had marched with armies towards the east, until he settled al-Ḥīra [Translator's note: the source has حير الحيرة, literally "he made al-Ḥīra a ḥīra (encampment)"], built Samarqand, and returned from the direction of the east. He made his way through Medina and found that his son, whom he had left there, had been treacherously killed, so he resolved to destroy it. The Anṣār would fight him by day and give him hospitality by night, and this pleased him. While he was thus, two rabbis from Qurayẓa came to him and persuaded him to abandon the fighting, and he entered their religion. Then he set out heading for Yemen, and on the way a group from Hudhayl met him and tempted him [to plunder] the Kaʿba; when he learned of their lie he killed them, and he went to the Kaʿba, clothed it, sacrificed six thousand camels, circumambulated and shaved his head. Then he left for Yemen and called his people to Islam, but they denied him.

safi-cedvel:40-42.t:
* I'rab:
(أجمعين) a genitive tawkīd (emphasis) in meaning (maʿnawī) of the pronoun in (ميقاتهم) ...
The clause «إنّ يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
41- (يوم) an accusative badal (substitute) of the first يوم; (لا) negative; (عن مولى) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يغني); (شيئا) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. anything of the punishment; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; the wāw in (ينصرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «لا يغني مولى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا هم ينصرون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا يغني.
The clause «ينصرون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
42- (إلّا) for exception; (من) in the position of nominative as badal of the nāʾib fāʿil [Note: Or of the first مولى.]; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is العزيز, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.. It may also be borrowed for the accusative position, as a tawkīd of the noun of إنّ.].
The clause «رحم الله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّه ... العزيز» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:43-50.t:
* I'rab:
(كالمهل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar of (إنّ) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of طعام الأثيم, the governing factor in it being the sense of emphasis in (إنّ).]; (في البطون) attached to (يغلي); (كغلي) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a boiling like the boiling of scalding water.
The clause «إنّ شجرة الزقّوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يغلي ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of المهل.
47- 50- (الفاء) conjunction; (إلى سواء) attached to (اعتلوه); (ثمّ) a conjunction; (فوق) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (صبّوا); (من عذاب) attached to (صبّوا); (أنت) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a pronoun borrowed for the accusative position, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إنّ.]; (ما) a relative noun, khabar of إنّ; (به) attached to (تمترون).
The clause «خذوه ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb [Note: I.e. Allah says to the keepers of Hell (al-zabāniya).].
The clause «اعتلوه ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause that is the object of speech.
The clause «صبّوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اعتلوه.
The clause «ذق ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb [Note: I.e. the keepers of Hell say to him.].
The clause «إنّك ... العزيز» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «إنّ هذا ما ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كنتم به تمترون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تمترون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(46) غلى: an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral غلى يغلي of the ḍaraba class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(49) ذق: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of being indeclinable on sukūn; its original is ذوق; the wāw was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

* Rhetoric:
1- Simile (tashbīh): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ طَعامُ الْأَثِيمِ، كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ الْحَمِيمِ».
For the zaqqūm is likened to copper melted by the action of fire, which is مهل, because it is left gradually (yumhal) in the fire until it melts. They describe every blameworthy food as boiling in the bellies — not literally; it is only figurative, as you say: rancour boils in his heart, and enmity boils in his breast.
2- Implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ الْحَمِيمِ».
For the punishment is likened to a liquid, and then pouring is imagined for it, as in his saying:
صبّت عليه صروف الدّهر من صبب
(The vicissitudes of time were poured upon him from a slope.)
and as in the words of Allah the Exalted «أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْراً». So He mentioned the punishment with pouring attached to it, borrowed for it, so that it would be more terrible and more awe-inspiring.
3- The figure of sarcasm (al-tahakkum): in the words of Allah the Exalted «ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ». This figure consists of using the language of good tidings in the place of warning, and of promise in the place of threat, out of the speaker's contempt for the one addressed and mockery of him; it is more galling to the one mocked and more painful to him.
For this noble verse came by way of mockery and sarcasm towards one who used to vaunt his might and nobility over his people.

safi-cedvel:51-57.t:
* I'rab:
(في مقام) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of إنّ; (في جنّات) a badal (substitute) of مقام with the preposition repeated; (من سندس) attached to (يلبسون).
The clause «إنّ المتّقين في مقام ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يلبسون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (إنّ).].
54- (كذلك) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus; (الواو) conjunction; (بحور) attached to (زوّجناهم).
The clause «الأمر كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «زوّجناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يلبسون.
55- (فيها) attached to (يدعون); (بكلّ) attached to (يدعون) by its being made to carry the meaning of يرغبون "they desire" (taḍmīn); (آمنين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يدعون.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (زوّجناهم).
56- 57- (لا) negative; (فيها) attached to (يذوقون); (إلّا) for exception; (الموتة) excepted, accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: Some said the exception is connected (muttaṣil), the interpretation being: the believer, at his death in this world, is as though in his place in Paradise, because of what he is given of it or because of what he becomes certain of regarding its bliss (Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal).]; (الواو) conjunction; (فضلا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with it in derivation, i.e. as a favour [Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) governed by وقاهم or يدعون.]; (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (فضلا); (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
The clause «لا يذوقون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil in (يدعون) or of the pronoun in (آمنين).
The clause «وقاهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause زوّجناهم, taking account of the iltifāt (shift of person).
The clause «ذلك ... الفوز» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(54) حور: plural of حوراء, feminine of أحور, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from حور يحور of the fariḥa class, i.e. the black of the eye became intense and its white became intense; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ».
أمين is from أمن (trustworthiness), which is the opposite of betrayal; the place is described by it by way of metaphor, as though a fearful place betrays its occupant because of the hardships he meets in it.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (بلسانك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسّرناه), and (الباء) is for accompaniment.
The clause «يسّرناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لعلّهم يتذكرون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتذكّرون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

* Rhetoric:
- The five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa).
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ. The verb يتذكرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). We shall set out below the most important points concerning the five verbs:
1- They are called the five verbs because we form five forms from the verb. The five verbs are every imperfect to which the dual alif, the plural wāw or the yāʾ of the (feminine) addressee is attached.
So from the verb يكتب we form the five verbs as follows: يكتبون - تكتبون - يكتبان - تكتبان - تكتبين.
2- The five verbs are made nominative by the retention of the nūn.
3- They are made accusative and jussive by the deletion of the nūn.
So I say: لم يكتبوا - لم تحفظي - لن تذهبوا - لن تنصرفا.
Remark: the dual alif, the plural wāw and the yāʾ of the addressee attached to the verb are in the position of nominative as fāʿil, or in the nominative as its noun if the verb is deficient (nāqiṣ) (i.e. kāna and its sisters).

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition.
The clause «ارتقب» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they disbelieve, then await their destruction.
The clause «إنّهم مرتقبون» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مرتقبون): plural of مرتقب, active participle of the five-letter ارتقب; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
